items.title: Michael Max Fleming interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, June 8, 2017
items.q: Everything he did was so spontaneous. You never knew what he was going to do. He never counted off the tunes. He never gave keys. He just started playing.

ctx.x: Were you more critical of your own playing because you knew you were going to hear it back? Did you play differently?

With him it was one thing, with him the records I made basically we played what we played on the gig. We didn’t write charts. I made up my parts. Nobody gave me a part. The whole group we just — it was a beautiful thing in a way. And so when we went into the studio I was nervous on that first record. But we were playing what we played every night. Everything he did was so spontaneous. You never knew what he was going to do. He never counted off the tunes. He never gave keys. He just started playing.
I just got this image of you and the piano player like, you know, one of you whispering to the other what key we’re in or something?
